objectives.text: Distinguish canon, institutional teaching, commentary, and historical evidence.

sources.title: Approaching Latter-day Saint Doctrine
sources.editorialNote: Church Newsroom guide (May 2007) on identifying doctrine.

questions.prompt: Which Article of Faith states that God “will yet reveal many great and important things pertaining to the Kingdom of God”?

options.text: Article of Faith 7
Article of Faith 8
Article of Faith 9
Article of Faith 10

questions.explanation: Article 9 affirms past, present and future revelation. Article 7 lists spiritual gifts such as revelation and prophecy, Article 8 concerns the Bible and Book of Mormon, and Article 10 concerns gathering, Zion and Christ's reign.

questions.prompt: Article of Faith 8 accepts the Bible as the word of God with which qualification?

options.text: As far as it is translated correctly
As far as it agrees with the Book of Mormon
As far as it is interpreted by Church leaders
As far as the New Testament is concerned

questions.explanation: The article's qualifier concerns translation. It does not make the Bible's authority depend on agreement with another book, on an interpreter, or on one testament.

questions.prompt: Article of Faith 11 claims the privilege of worshiping according to one's own conscience and allows all others the same privilege.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Article 11 claims this privilege and extends it to all people, “let them worship how, where, or what they may.”

questions.prompt: According to Article of Faith 5, how must a man be called to preach the gospel and administer its ordinances?

options.text: By a vote of the local congregation
By prophecy and the laying on of hands by those in authority
By completing a course of religious study
By a personal experience of conversion

questions.explanation: Article 5 names being called of God by prophecy and by the laying on of hands by those who are in authority. The article mentions none of the other options.

questions.prompt: A friend says the Articles of Faith are a complete summary of Latter-day Saint doctrine. Which response best fits the text?

options.text: Yes; Article 13 states that the list is complete
No; they are commentary rather than scripture
They state core beliefs briefly, and Article 9 itself expects further revelation
They summarize the Book of Mormon only

questions.explanation: The thirteen articles are short canonical statements of belief, and Article 9 anticipates more revelation, so they are not presented as exhaustive. Article 13 concerns conduct and virtue; the articles are canonical, in the Pearl of Great Price; and they are not a Book of Mormon summary.

sourceLocators.locator: The standard works: an open canon

questions.prompt: The Articles of Faith are part of the Pearl of Great Price, one of the standard works.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The thirteen Articles of Faith are printed in the Pearl of Great Price. The Church's guide also names them separately among the sources of doctrine.

questions.prompt: In Doctrine and Covenants 68:4, what is said to “be scripture”?

options.text: Every word spoken by an ordained elder
Whatever they speak when moved upon by the Holy Ghost
Anything printed in a Church publication
Every sermon that is recorded in writing

questions.explanation: Verse 4 ties this broad sense of scripture to being moved upon by the Holy Ghost. It does not make ordination, publication or a written record the condition.

questions.prompt: Doctrine and Covenants 1:38 says, “whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.” What does the verse claim?

options.text: That the Lord's word, given by his own voice or through his servants, will be fulfilled
That anyone who speaks about God speaks for him
That servants' words replace earlier scripture
That only words spoken aloud count as revelation

questions.explanation: The verse affirms that the Lord's word shall all be fulfilled, whether given by his own voice or his servants'. It does not extend this to anyone who speaks about God, say later words replace scripture, or limit revelation to speech.

questions.prompt: Doctrine and Covenants 68:1–3 first addresses Orson Hyde and presents his calling as an “ensample” for others ordained to the priesthood.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Verse 1 names Orson Hyde; verses 2–3 call this an ensample to those ordained to this priesthood, who are to speak as moved upon by the Holy Ghost.

questions.prompt: Doctrine and Covenants 68:4 says that inspired words spoken by Church leaders are added to the standard works.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The verse calls such inspired speech scripture in a broad sense, the will, mind, word and voice of the Lord, but says nothing about the standard works. Additions to the canon happen by a separate, formal process presented to the Church.

sourceLocators.locator: Institutional teaching: how the Church speaks today

questions.prompt: Read alongside D&C 68:4, what does the Church's guide add about statements by Church leaders?

options.text: That every leader's sermon becomes doctrine once it is published
That a single statement by one leader on one occasion is often a personal view, not binding on the Church
That members should disregard what leaders say outside general conference
That only the Bible should be treated as scripture

questions.explanation: The guide says not every statement by a leader is doctrine and that a single statement on one occasion often represents a personal, considered opinion. It does not say publication makes a sermon doctrine, tell members to disregard leaders, or limit scripture to the Bible.

questions.prompt: In Doctrine and Covenants 1:39, what does the Spirit do?

options.text: It beareth record, and the record is true
It replaces the need for scripture
It speaks only to the President of the Church
It confirms every statement made in the Church

questions.explanation: Verse 39 says the Spirit beareth record and the record is true, and the truth abides forever. It does not say the Spirit replaces scripture, speaks to one person only, or confirms every statement.

questions.prompt: Doctrine and Covenants 1:37 invites readers to search “these commandments.”

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Verse 37 opens, “Search these commandments, for they are true and faithful.”

questions.prompt: According to the Church's guide, who establishes the Church's doctrine?

options.text: Any General Authority speaking in general conference
The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, counseling together
Faculty in Church-sponsored universities
Each local bishop for his own ward

questions.explanation: The guide names the First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve, counseling together. A conference speaker, scholars and local leaders teach, but the guide does not give them this role.

questions.prompt: Which list matches the guide's description of where the Church's doctrine resides?

options.text: The standard works, official declarations and proclamations, and the Articles of Faith
General conference talks, Church magazines and devotional books
Seminary manuals and Church history volumes
Popular books by Church leaders

questions.explanation: The guide names the four standard works, official declarations and proclamations, and the Articles of Faith. It adds that doctrine is consistently proclaimed in official publications, but it does not list magazines, manuals or books as the place doctrine resides.

questions.prompt: Which example does the guide give of a peripheral teaching that should not be treated as central?

options.text: The Atonement of Jesus Christ
The Resurrection of Jesus Christ
The location of the Garden of Eden
Faith in Jesus Christ

questions.explanation: The guide contrasts core doctrines, such as the Atonement, with peripheral ones, using the location of the Garden of Eden as its example. The Resurrection and faith in Christ belong to the core it describes.

questions.prompt: The Church's guide says its doctrine is consistently proclaimed in official Church publications.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The guide states that doctrine established by the First Presidency and the Twelve is consistently proclaimed in official Church publications.

questions.prompt: A blog post quotes a nineteenth-century sermon to prove a “Mormon doctrine.” Following the guide, which question should you ask first?

options.text: How many times has the quote been shared online?
Did the speaker hold a high office in the Church?
Is the teaching found in the standard works, official declarations, or current official publications?
Does the sermon sound inspired to me?

questions.explanation: The guide points to the standard works, official declarations and proclamations, and consistent official publications. Popularity proves nothing; a speaker's office alone does not make a single statement doctrine; and a personal impression does not settle the source's standing.

sourceLocators.locator: Statements by individual leaders; sources of doctrine

questions.prompt: The Church's guide says some doctrines are more central than others.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes core doctrines, such as the Atonement of Jesus Christ, from peripheral ones.

questions.prompt: Why does the guide say some disagreements about Latter-day Saint belief arise?

options.text: Members are not allowed to explain their beliefs
Some terms carry different meanings in Latter-day Saint usage than in other traditions
The standard works contradict each other
Doctrine changes every year

questions.explanation: The guide notes that terms can carry different meanings, giving being “born again” as an example. It does not claim the other reasons.

questions.prompt: Which category best fits a current Gospel Topics page on the Church's website?

options.text: Canonical scripture
Institutional explanation
Individual commentary
Historical record

questions.explanation: A Church-published explanation shows how the Church teaches a subject today. It is not part of the standard works, it is not one author's private interpretation, and it is not a record of a past event.
questions.perspective: Original Hearken reading method grounded in the cited sources

questions.prompt: How does this course classify a general conference address published by the Church?

options.text: Canonical scripture, once it is printed
Institutional teaching, but not part of the standard works
Personal commentary with no institutional standing
A historical record only

questions.explanation: Conference addresses are delivered and published by the Church and show how it teaches. They are not added to the standard works by being printed, and treating them as mere private commentary or only as history would understate their role.
questions.perspective: Original Hearken reading method grounded in the cited sources

questions.prompt: James E. Talmage published The Articles of Faith in 1899 and later served as an apostle. How should a careful student cite the book?

options.text: As canonical scripture
As an official declaration
As historical commentary, useful for context, that does not settle current teaching
As the Church's current explanation of every article

questions.explanation: The book is one learned author's explanation in his era. Its author's later office does not make it canon or an official declaration, and an 1899 commentary cannot stand in for current institutional teaching.
questions.perspective: Original Hearken reading method grounded in the cited sources

questions.prompt: Why does the source ledger record a source's setting?

options.text: Because a source's meaning and reach depend on who said it, when, to whom and why
Because older sources always outrank newer ones
Because the setting decides whether a source is true
Because only sources with a known setting may be quoted

questions.explanation: Setting tells you what a source can show: a revelation addressed to one person, a conference address and a private letter carry different reach. Age does not determine rank, setting does not decide truth, and sources without full settings can still be used with care.
questions.perspective: Original Hearken reading method grounded in the cited sources

questions.prompt: A dated diary entry reports what its writer heard at an 1880 meeting. What does it most directly establish?

options.text: What the Church teaches today
What the writer reported hearing at that meeting
That the idea was official doctrine in 1880
That every member present agreed

questions.explanation: A diary is a historical record of what its writer reported. By itself it does not show doctrinal status then or now, or the views of others present.
questions.perspective: Original Hearken reading method grounded in the cited sources

sourceLocators.locator: Historical records: what someone said, when

questions.prompt: Which event shows that the Latter-day Saint canon is open?

options.text: Two revelations were accepted into scripture by a general conference in 1976 and became D&C 137 and 138
A popular book was quoted in many sacrament meetings
A Church magazine printed a new article
A historian discovered an early diary

questions.explanation: The 1976 additions were presented to a general conference and accepted, and in 1981 became sections 137 and 138. Quotation, magazine publication and historical discovery do not change the canon.

questions.title: Where doctrine comes from
questions.prompt: Match each item from the Church's guide to its description.
questions.instructions: Match each item on the left to exactly one description on the right. Use every description once.

leftItems.text: The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve
A single statement by one leader on one occasion
The location of the Garden of Eden

rightItems.text: Often a personal view, not binding on the Church
The Bible, Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price
The guide's example of a peripheral teaching
The councils that establish doctrine together

questions.explanation: Each description follows the guide: the four standard works, the councils that establish doctrine, the caution about single statements, and its example of a peripheral subject.

sourceLocators.locator: Sources of doctrine; individual statements; central and peripheral doctrines

presentation.accessibility: Every pair must be makeable by tapping a left item, then a right item; dragging is optional.
